item.title: Meta to Pay Up to $17.1 Billion in Landmark Settlement Over Social Media Addiction Claims
item.description: The social media giant settled with 47 states, the District of Columbia and U.S. territories, and agreed to make major changes to its products over claims its platforms endangered children.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang and Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Meta headquarters in California.

item.title: What to Know About Social Media Addiction Lawsuits Against Meta, Snap, TikTok and YouTube
item.description: Landmark trials are testing a new legal strategy claiming that Meta, TikTok, Snap and YouTube caused personal injury through addictive products.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: David Gray/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: The lawsuits are for the first time putting social media companies on the spot for creating harmful products, exposing them to new kinds of liability.

item.title: Bessent Faces Credibility Test in Quest to Tame Markets
item.description: The Treasury secretary is confronting the limits of his ability to reshape the economy ahead of midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston/The New York Times
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is starting to see the limits of his powers to bend the market to his will.

item.title: ‘Honeymoon’s Over’: Warsh Under Pressure as Fed Weighs Raising Rates
item.description: Kevin M. Warsh is scheduled to deliver his first address at the Federal Reserve’s annual conference in Jackson, Wyo., with U.S. government bond markets on edge and inflation risks resurfacing.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:credit: Anna Rose Layden for The New York Times
item.media:description: Kevin M. Warsh, the Federal Reserve chairman.

item.title: Diesel Price Nears Record High, Helping Oil Companies and Hurting Consumers
item.description: The cost of the fuel, used in farm machinery, trucks and other heavy equipment, has surged because of the war in Iran and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.
item.dc:creator: Aruni Soni
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Kristen Zeis for The New York Times
item.media:description: The average cost of diesel, used by trucks that transport goods, has risen since the start of the war with Iran.

item.title: PCE Index Shows Inflation Remained Elevated in July Amid High Energy Costs
item.description: The Personal Consumption Expenditure index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation tracker, held steady in July.
item.dc:creator: Ben Casselman
item.media:credit: Joe Raedle/Getty Images
item.media:description: Many households are struggling to manage higher prices.

item.title: Even as Trump’s Standing Slips, He Slingshots Darline Graham to Victory
item.description: After facing low approval ratings and endorsement setbacks, the president made a show of force in lifting Darline Graham to the Republican nomination for Senate in South Carolina.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies and Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump hosted a rally on Friday in Myrtle Beach, S.C., for Senator Darline Graham, part of a full-court press on her behalf.

item.title: Graham, and Trump, Triumph: Six Takeaways From South Carolina’s Senate Runoff
item.description: President Trump went all in for Senator Darline Graham in a primary runoff on Tuesday. It worked, preserving his undefeated streak in Republican Senate primaries this year.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Sean Rayford for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham’s victory on Tuesday showed President Trump’s continued ability to move Republican primary voters, especially when he goes all in on a race.

item.title: In Headache for Republicans, Second Dan Sullivan Advances in Alaska Senate Race
item.description: A long-shot candidate with the same name as the incumbent Republican senator will be on the ballot in November. That could be a problem for the G.O.P.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Christopher Miller for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dan J. Sullivan in Petersburg, Alaska, this summer.

item.title: Joe Manchin Pushes for More Independents to Join Congress
item.description: The former Democratic-turned-independent senator and his daughter are backing independent bids for the House and the Senate to try to weaken the two-party grip on the Capitol.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:credit: Jason Andrew for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former Senator Joe Manchin III and his daughter Heather said they believe the door is open given growing public disillusionment with partisan stalemate and party politics.

item.title: Dolly Parton Had the Voice, and Concerns, of an Earth Angel
item.description: Parton gave hopeful expression to songs she wrote about the hard times and hard-won triumphs of her life.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Zoladz
item.media:credit: Ron Davis/Getty Images
item.media:description: Some of Parton’s most celebrated songs recounted scenes from her life, told with cinematic detail.

item.title: Dolly Parton: A Life in Pictures
item.description: Parton made her mark in the country arenas of Nashville, and then crossed over into the pop world, Hollywood and beyond.
item.dc:creator: Melena Ryzik
item.media:credit: Paul Natkin/Getty Images

item.title: As CTE Cases Soar, Why Can’t Americans Quit the NFL?
item.description: A collision of American popular culture and public health is on display in the N.F.L.
item.dc:creator: John Branch
item.media:credit: Mark Makela for The New York Times
item.media:description: According to a new study, about 25 percent of the nearly 900 former N.F.L. players who died between 2016 and 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy.

item.title: ‘You’re Ruining My Dreams’: C.T.E. Study Adds to Family Tension Over Football
item.description: Many families are engaged in tense debates after a new study found a high percentage of N.F.L. players had developed degenerative brain disease.
item.dc:creator: Juliet Macur
item.media:credit: Gabriella Angotti-Jones for The New York Times
item.media:description: For parents, the new C.T.E. study layered fear, uncertainty and guilt onto an already difficult situation.

item.title: 5 Takeaways on the Fallout From an Alarming C.T.E. Study
item.description: At least one in four N.F.L. players, and likely a much higher percentage, had the brain disease when they died. Will anything change?
item.dc:creator: John Branch
item.media:credit: Kristian Thacker for The New York Times
item.media:description: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy can be diagnosed only posthumously.

item.title: F.D.A. Approves the Drug Daraxonrasib That’s Poised to Transform Pancreatic Cancer
item.description: In a key clinical trial, patients who got the pill, daraxonrasib, lived twice as long as those who got chemotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Gina Kolata and Rebecca Robbins
item.media:credit: Kim Raff for The New York Times
item.media:description: Daraxonrasib, the first drug of its type, has electrified pancreatic cancer specialists and patients because it has shown it can double life expectancy.

item.title: Tim Curry, Star of ‘Rocky Horror Picture Show,’ Dies at 80
item.description: The actor’s gift for garish eccentricity was indelibly appropriate for the outlandish, cross-dressing mad scientist Frank-N-Furter.
item.dc:creator: Bruce Weber
item.media:credit: Evening Standard/Hulton Archive/Getty Images
item.media:description: Tim Curry in 1974, the year he starred in the premiere American production of “The Rocky Horror Show” in Los Angeles.

item.title: Deadly Nepal Flood May Have Been Caused by ‘Ice Avalanche,’ Scientists Say
item.description: An initial assessment of satellite imagery suggests an “ice avalanche” from a high-altitude glacier sent a giant cascade into the valley below.
item.dc:creator: Leo Sands
item.media:credit: Prakash Mathema/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: A glacial lake in the Everest region of Nepal, in 2018.

item.title: In Canada and at Home, Deference to Trump Turns to Defiance on Tariffs and Other Issues
item.description: While the president remains the most dominant figure in the world, other leaders and institutions are pushing back more vigorously than at the beginning of his second term.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston/The New York Times
item.media:description: World leaders and domestic institutions are showing less willingness to submit to President Trump’s will.

item.title: Canadians Stand Their Ground Amid New Trump Tariffs and Expanding U.S.-Canada Trade War
item.description: Business owners are preparing for financial pain after the latest U.S.-Canada trade talks collapsed. But many Canadians are embracing a show of resistance.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:credit: Nick Iwanyshyn/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Of Canadian politicians’ responses to the trade war, perhaps the most colorful came from Doug Ford, the premier of Ontario, on Monday.

item.title: At Trump’s IndyCar Race, a V.I.P. Invitation Became a Diplomatic Snub
item.description: Foreign ambassadors were promised free food and drinks, misting fans and shaded seats during the event. Then some of them were uninvited.
item.dc:creator: Anton Troianovski and Eric Schmitt
item.media:credit: Anna Rose Layden for The New York Times
item.media:description: White House staff members watch the Freedom 250 Grand Prix on the National Mall last week. Some ambassadors were uninvited.

item.title: Ukraine’s Most Potent Weapon: The Software Orchestrating Its Drone Army
item.description: The Delta system pulls together battlefield data to identify targets, creating a miles-wide “kill zone.” The technology is credited with helping to cut Russian advances to a near standstill.
item.dc:creator: Constant Méheut and Olha Konovalova
item.media:credit: Tyler Hicks/The New York Times
item.media:description: Officers from Ukraine’s First Separate Assault Regiment looking at live battlefield footage from drones, displayed through the Delta system, at a command bunker in eastern Ukraine in 2025.

item.title: Under Threat, Saudi Arabia Reroutes Oil Exports Yet Again
item.description: Forced away from the Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf, the Saudis turned to the Red Sea. Now they are relying on a less dangerous but more complicated detour via the Suez Canal.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Shokry Hussien/Reuters
item.media:description: A container terminal in Ain Sokhna, Egypt. Saudi tankers offload oil in Ain Sokhna for the Sumed pipeline, which connects to the Mediterranean.

item.title: Oil Prices Dip on News of Progress in Hormuz Talks
item.description: Iran and Oman said they would create a temporary shipping lane and clear mines in the waterway. Global oil prices eased after the joint announcement.
item.dc:creator: Lara Jakes
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Reuters
item.media:description: Vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, seen from Musandam, Oman, on Monday. Before the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, about a fifth of the world’s oil and gas was shipped through the waterway.

item.title: With ‘Killer in the Code,’ Michael Connelly Puts His Reputation on the Line
item.description: The novelist Michael Connelly knows he is putting his reputation on the line with the podcast “Killer in the Code.” But despite critics’ skepticism, he finds the evidence “completely convincing.”
item.dc:creator: Alexander Nazaryan
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Michael Connelly, a reporter turned novelist, has created iconic characters like Harry Bosch and Mickey Haller, otherwise known as the Lincoln Lawyer.

item.title: Bill Gates Is Warning That A.I. Is More Dangerous Than Big Tech Will Admit
item.description: In an hourlong interview, he said his industry was downplaying the risks, which he believes include mass unemployment and bioterrorism.
item.dc:creator: Karen Weise
item.media:credit: Chona Kasinger for The New York Times
item.media:description: Bill Gates is the latest in a string of tech luminaries to call out the risks of artificial intelligence.

item.title: A Surrogate Refused an Abortion and Fled to Texas. Now She Wants Custody of the Baby.

item.media:credit: LM Otero/Associated Press
item.media:description: McKenna West, right, after a court hearing in Dallas on Tuesday.
